title: preASSIST Study - Preparation for AI-powered Surveillance Systems for Immuno- and Systemic Therapies
summary:
In a previous study (CoMMoD-CAST), we showed that continuous, non-invasive monitoring of vital signs and physical activity using wearable devices can automatically detect severe clinical complications (SCC) in blood cancer patients undergoing treatment. However, the methods used in the study were cumbersome for both patients and healthcare professionals, limiting the ability to scale the system. To address this, we developed an advanced data management platform (monti), which allows data from wearables and patient-generated information (such as electronic reports) to be directly transferred into a database.
Intensive chemotherapy, alone or combined with stem cell transplants and/or immunotherapies, can offer a potential cure for blood cancers like leukemia, lymphoproliferative disorders, and autoimmune diseases. However, these treatments can lead to life-threatening complications such as infections, bleeding, heart issues, and immune reactions. Early detection of these complications is essential, as delayed treatment can lead to serious illness or death. Nearly every patient undergoing these treatments experiences at least one severe complication. Currently, hospital monitoring relies on intermittent checks of vital signs, daily clinical exams, and lab tests, which are done several times a day in the hospital and during regular visits for outpatients.
Because there is no continuous monitoring, complications such as infections, cytokine release syndrome, or heart and lung failure may only be detected late, making treatment more difficult. Combining wearable monitoring with patient-generated data could help detect these complications earlier. Continuous digital monitoring could also reduce the workload for specialized nursing staff.
conditions: Patients receiving chemotherapy and/or immunotherapy for malignant and non-malignant diseases.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Patients receiving chemotherapy and/or immunotherapy for malignant and non-malignant diseases
• Aged ≥18 and able to understand the design and objectives of the study
• Signed informed consent and data protection agreement prior to any study-related activities
• Willingness to wear the wearable during the treatment period and return it at a follow-up visit
Exclusion criteria:
• Medical or mental conditions (e.g., dementia) that impair the ability to wear the wearable or use the smartphone during the treatment period
• Active implants (e.g., pacemakers)
• Skin diseases or defects at the site of the wearable
• Allergy to the wearable or its components (e.g., synthetic materials)
• Conditions that exclude wearing a wearable (e.g., shunts, active bleeding)
• History of non-functional hemoglobin (e.g., sickle cell anemia, recent carbon monoxide poisoning)
• Language barriers preventing adequate understanding or cooperation, individuals known or suspected of non-compliance with study instructions, or individuals who, in the investigator's opinion, should not participate in the study
